title: How do we remove the bracket from five hundred minus a difference?
description: The expression five hundred minus the bracket two hundred and fifty minus one hundred is written without the bracket, by finding how much too much is taken away. Keeko's doubt is that dropping the bracket gives five hundred minus two hundred and fifty minus one hundred.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking away a difference takes away less, so the second number must be added back. Ask the child to check the new expression against working the bracket first.

source: Consider 500 − (250 − 100). Can we write it as 500 − 250 − 1
video_script.why: The child sees a bracket after a minus sign removed by finding what was taken away too much, so the signs inside change.
video_script.substitution: Change the three numbers and the method stays the same: take away the first, then add back what was taken away too much.
video_script.anchor: a bar of five hundred units with two hundred and fifty marked off and one hundred marked as given back
video_script.wrong_answer: we drop the bracket and write five hundred minus two hundred and fifty minus one hundred
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko drops the bracket and keeps the signs inside, so one hundred too much is taken away.
video_script.payoff_line: The value is three hundred and fifty, and the bracket is removed by changing the signs inside.

final_answer.spoken: five hundred minus the bracket two hundred and fifty minus one hundred is five hundred minus two hundred and fifty plus one hundred, which is three hundred and fifty

maths_rules: taking away 250 takes away 100 too much, so add back 100: 500 - 250 + 100
the signs of 250 and -100 change to -250 and +100
video_script.design: One idea: taking away a difference takes away less, so the part that was too much is added back. The bar stays in the anchor band; the working band shows each step. Keeko's doubt: drop the bracket and keep the signs.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expression without the bracket that has the same value

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to write it without the bracket, so that the value stays the same.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, work out the bracket first.
Two hundred and fifty minus one hundred is one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five hundred minus one hundred and fifty is three hundred and fifty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 500 − 250 = 250; this has taken away 100 more than needed

marks.m2: the extra 100 taken away is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, take away two hundred and fifty directly from five hundred.
That leaves two hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But that takes away one hundred more than we needed to.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, give back the extra hundred by adding it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The expression is five hundred minus two hundred and fifty plus one hundred.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 500 − 250 + 100 = 350, the same as 500 − 150; the signs of 250 and −100 changed to −250 and +100

marks.m2: the signs of 250 and −100 are shown changing to −250 and +100

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, two hundred and fifty plus one hundred is three hundred and fifty.
That matches what we found by working the bracket first.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The signs inside the bracket have changed.
Plus two hundred and fifty became minus two hundred and fifty.
Minus one hundred became plus one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>The value is three hundred and fifty, and the bracket is removed by changing the signs inside.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It is not five hundred minus two hundred and fifty minus one hundred.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>But that takes away one hundred too much.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Only two hundred and fifty minus one hundred is taken away.
